newsitem.title: USA: Alternate Postal to cut Q4 overhead.
newsitem.headline: Alternate Postal to cut Q4 overhead.

text.p: Alternate Postal Delivery Inc said Friday it planned to make "selected cuts" in overhead in the fourth quarter to offset an expected decline in magazine revenue.

The company said it was anticipating lower magazine revenue until the next U.S. Postal Service rate increase, which is expected to be considered in 1998, Phillip Miller, the company's president, said in a statement. Alternate Postal provides private delivery services.
Earlier, the company reported a third-quarter loss of $0.12 a share, compared with a loss of $0.28 in the year-earlier period.
The company said its 1996 third-quarter loss reflected a decrease in revenue from product sample programs, with only client test programs being executed during the period.
In addition, lower magazine revenues resulted from discounts offered to large-volume publishers by the U.S. Postal Service.
Alternate Postal said it recently entered into an alliance with News America FSI, a division of News Corp.
"We believe that the new alliance with News America FSI should go far in building revenues in 1997," Miller said.
